cases.name: sort-feature-prop-asc
cases.comment: Concrete feature-property sort (the sort lateral binds path = wpath = the concrete wpath to use the full search_flat key prefix). zsort-a/-d hold arrays (ASC sorts by the MIN element), zsort-b also has feature meter2 with reading 1, so the /features/*/properties/reading twin rows carry a smaller value than its own meter reading (5) and must not leak into the sort, zsort-c misses the key (null rank, first) although its meter2 twin rows carry 99, zsort-e is a string (after all numbers). Sort keys carry no auth on either backend (plan §3.3 exception 3), so every auth situation must agree, incl. 'limited' (features revoked). The zsort-* ids sort after every other pre-SB-02 parity id (the SB-02 zzempty-* ids sort after them for the same reason) so first-page-pinned divergence lists (not-wildcard-eq) stay stable, and every zsort feature carries status "on" (so only the full eq-wildcard-status-on pin lists them; the empty(features/*/...) divergence a feature WITHOUT status once tripped in empty-wildcard-property -- Mongo matched a thing with a feature that lacks the property, Postgres did not -- was closed by SB-02).

cases.name: sort-feature-prop-desc
cases.comment: DESC twin of sort-feature-prop-asc: arrays sort by their MAX element, the missing key sorts last. zsort-c's meter2 reading 99 is larger than every meter reading, so a leak of the /features/* twin rows would move zsort-c from last to first.

cases.name: walk-rank-asc
cases.comment: Walks the dedicated single-type-bracket walker corpus: missing-value things exercise the null-sort-value resume branch (D4 review gap), int/long/double values cross the numeric sub-type boundaries and the 42/42 tie exercises the eq-dimension resume. Mixed-type brackets are NOT cursor-crossable on EITHER backend (shared upstream type-bracketed gt/lt limitation, see PostgresCursorResumeIT), and explicit-null sort values duplicate on both backends after a null boundary (exists(key) matches explicit null), so those stay in the SORT battery (sort-rank-asc/desc) but out of the walks.

cases.name: walk-feature-level-asc
cases.comment: Cursor walk on a concrete feature-property sort key: the three f1 things without a level exercise the null-anchor resume branch, the 3/3 tie the eq-dimension resume. Scalars only (no arrays, no explicit nulls), per the walk-corpus rules in SearchBackendParityIT.

cases.name: walk-rankdiv-asc-divergent-encodings
cases.comment: Pins each backend's OBSERVED walk over container-valued sort keys: the divergent cursor sort-value encodings (Mongo: whole array; Postgres: null for rank-4/5 boundaries) plus type-bracketed resume predicates make each backend drop a DIFFERENT subset mid-walk. The unpaged-reference invariant is deliberately not applied to pinned walks (see SearchBackendParityIT.runCursorWalkComparison).

cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), /definition path (slash-mapped simple field): not(in(p,v,null)) is the complement of value-or-null-or-missing -- only a leaf that EXISTS with a different value (nenull-stringvals) matches.

cases.name: in-thingid-value-null
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), root-mapped thingId (Mongo _id, Postgres column; never null, never missing): in(thingId,v,null) matches exactly the listed id -- the null member can match nothing.

cases.name: ge-thingid-null
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), root-mapped thingId: ge(thingId,null) = {_id:null} matches NOTHING because _id is never null nor missing (the thing-level counterparts ge-attr-nullattr-null etc. DO match missing leaves).

cases.name: gt-thingid-null
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), root-mapped thingId: gt(thingId,null) matches NOTHING on both backends.

cases.name: not-gt-namespace-null
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), root-mapped namespace: not(gt(namespace,null)) matches every visible thing (negation of a never-matching predicate).

cases.name: in-namespace-value-null
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), root-mapped namespace: in(namespace,v,null) matches exactly the things of the listed namespace -- the null member can match nothing (namespace is never null nor missing).

cases.name: and-in-nullattr-value-null-eq-color-red
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), selective-leg shape: and(in(p,v,null), eq(color,red)) -- scalars-red and parityb-red (nullAttr MISSING, color red) match; the in() with a null member is not a point leg, eq(color) is.

cases.name: and-in-nullattr-value-null-exists-size
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), selective-leg shape: and(in(p,v,null), exists(size)) -- no point leg at all (in() carries null, exists never is one); every thing with a size attribute and a missing/null/listed nullAttr matches.

cases.name: and-eq-color-red-in-nullattr-null
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), selective-leg shape: and(eq(color,red), in(p,null)) -- eq(color) is the point leg; in(p,null) (null OR missing) must not be hoisted; scalars-red and parityb-red match.

cases.name: count-in-attr-nullattr-value-null
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), count mode: in(p,v,null) counts the listed value, the JSON-null leaf and every MISSING leaf (everything but nenull-stringvals).

cases.name: not-ge-attr-nullattr-null
cases.comment: null-operand Mongo-parity battery (SB-01), attribute path: not(ge(p,null)) is the complement of null-or-missing -- only a leaf that EXISTS with a non-null value matches (nenull-realvals, nenull-stringvals), like ne(p,null).

cases.name: empty-wildcard-brightness
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), feature-property path: Mongo elemMatch(f, and(or(eq(properties.brightness,null),eq([]),eq({}),eq("")), auth)) and $eq:null also matches a MISSING key, so a thing matches when at least one VISIBLE feature lacks brightness or holds an empty marker (scalars-red: sensor lacks it); a thing without features never matches. Before SB-02 PostgreSQL probed only rows AT the wildcard wpath, so a feature without the key could not match. The SB-02 corpus things are named zzempty-* so they sort after zsort-e and leave every first-page pin untouched; being feature-bearing without nullProp they join the complete PostgreSQL pins of in/ge/le-wildcard-nullprop-* (null = missing), which SB-02 extended.

cases.name: not-empty-wildcard-brightness
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the complement, page 1 (25) under sort(-thingId) so the zzempty-* things lead the compared page: Mongo $nor[elemMatch(f, and(empty, auth))] = NO visible feature lacks brightness or holds an empty marker there. Two shapes the MongoDB system-test run confirmed: a thing WITHOUT any feature matches (vacuously), and a thing with two features of which one holds brightness and the other lacks it (scalars-red, scalars-blue: lamp holds it, sensor lacks it) does NOT match although a visible feature has a non-empty brightness; no feature-bearing thing carries brightness on every feature, so the page holds the 25 highest-sorting feature-less things (walker-*, unicode, rankdiv-*, rank-*, range-*). The translation is the plain NOT of the per-feature EXISTS, never a positive some-feature-has-a-value probe.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-obj
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), object-valued property (item 1b): zzempty-full (its only feature holds obj = {"a":1}) must NOT match -- Mongo's eq({}) matches only the empty object, so the wildcard form needs the same deeper-path anti-probe as the concrete form, scoped to the feature; zzempty-hollow (obj = {}) and every feature lacking obj match. Auth coupling: under 'feature' zzempty-graded-unseen matches (its visible f1 lacks obj although the invisible f2 holds one) and zzempty-graded-seen does not (its visible f1 holds obj; the lacking f2 is invisible).

cases.name: not-empty-wildcard-obj
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the complement, page 1 (25) under sort(-thingId) so the zzempty-* things lead the compared page: zzempty-full (its only feature holds obj = {"a":1}, so it is NOT empty -- the 1b anti-probe under negation) leads, then the feature-less things; zzempty-split (f1 obj = {}), zzempty-hollow ({}) and every thing with a feature lacking obj are excluded; under 'feature' only zzempty-graded-seen (the one policy-graded thing whose visible feature holds a non-empty obj).

cases.name: empty-and-exists-wildcard-obj
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the empty-object branch next to exists(): zzempty-hollow (obj = {} present and empty) matches; the two wildcard terms are separate elemMatch/EXISTS probes on both backends, so a thing with one feature lacking obj and another holding one (zzempty-graded-*) matches too.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-props
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), bare /properties: a feature without properties (zzempty-shapes defonly, void) or with properties = {} (zzempty-shapes blank) matches, a feature with at least one property does not -- before SB-02 PostgreSQL matched EVERY feature with properties here (the object row exists and the wildcard form had no deeper-path anti-probe).

cases.name: not-empty-wildcard-props
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the complement, page 1 (25) under sort(-thingId) so the zzempty-* things lead the compared page: every thing whose visible features ALL have at least one property (zzempty-split, zzempty-markers, zzempty-hollow, both zzempty-graded-*, zzempty-full, zsort-*, ...) leads, then the feature-less things; zzempty-shapes (defonly/void without properties, blank with {}) is excluded.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-desired
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), bare /desiredProperties: missing on every pre-SB-02 feature and {} on zzempty-shapes blank; zzempty-full and zzempty-hollow (their desiredProperties hold target) do not match -- before SB-02 PostgreSQL matched them (the object row exists, no feature-scoped anti-probe).

cases.name: not-empty-wildcard-desired
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the complement, page 1 (25) under sort(-thingId) so the zzempty-* things lead the compared page: zzempty-hollow (desiredProperties hold target = {}: the container itself is non-empty) and zzempty-full (target, cfg) lead -- the 1b anti-probe on the bare container under negation -- then the feature-less things; zzempty-split (f1 desiredProperties = {}), the zzempty-graded-* (one feature lacks them) and every pre-SB-02 thing (none has desiredProperties) are excluded.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-target
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), desired-property path: missing on every feature but zzempty-full (5), zzempty-hollow ({} matches) and one feature of each zzempty-graded-* thing.

cases.name: not-empty-wildcard-target
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the complement, page 1 (25) under sort(-thingId) so the zzempty-* things lead the compared page: zzempty-full (target = 5) leads, then the feature-less things; zzempty-hollow (target = {}), zzempty-split (f1 lacks target) and every other feature-bearing thing are excluded.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-definition
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), /definition path: a feature without a definition matches (every pre-SB-02 feature, zzempty-shapes void and blank, zzempty-hollow); zzempty-full (its only feature is defined) does not; the zzempty-graded-* things follow the visible feature under 'feature'.

cases.name: not-empty-wildcard-definition
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the complement, page 1 (25) under sort(-thingId) so the zzempty-* things lead the compared page: zzempty-full (its only feature is defined) leads, then the feature-less things; zzempty-shapes (void/blank undefined) and every other feature-bearing thing are excluded.

cases.name: and-empty-wildcard-obj-eq-color-red
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), next to a point leg (the selective-leg CTE path): scalars-red (lamp and sensor lack obj).

cases.name: count-empty-wildcard-brightness
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), count mode of empty-wildcard-brightness: the same per-feature probe under the count statement.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-desired-cfg
cases.comment:
empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), object-valued DESIRED property (item 1b on the desiredProperties/

shape): zzempty-full (its only feature holds cfg = {"mode":"auto"}) must NOT match -- before SB-02 PostgreSQL matched it (object row at the wildcard wpath, no anti-probe); every feature lacking cfg matches.

cases.name: not-empty-wildcard-desired-cfg
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the complement, page 1 (25) under sort(-thingId) so the zzempty-* things lead the compared page: zzempty-full (cfg = {"mode":"auto"}, the 1b anti-probe under negation: a non-empty object IS in the complement) leads, then the feature-less things; every other feature-bearing thing has a feature lacking cfg and is excluded.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-nul
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), JSON-null marker on a wildcard path: Mongo eq(properties.nul, null) inside elemMatch. zzempty-markers (its ONLY feature holds nul = null) can match only through the type_rank = 1 branch of the same-feature row -- the isolating witness; zzempty-shapes (markers feature) and every feature lacking nul match as well.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-str
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), empty-string marker on a wildcard path: Mongo eq(properties.str, "") inside elemMatch. zzempty-markers (its ONLY feature holds str = "") can match only through the val_text = '' branch -- the isolating witness; every feature lacking str matches as well.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-arr
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), empty-array marker on a wildcard path: Mongo eq(properties.arr, []) inside elemMatch. zzempty-markers (its ONLY feature holds arr = []) can match only through the type_rank = 5 (empty-array stub) branch -- the isolating witness; every feature lacking arr matches as well.

cases.name: not-empty-wildcard-arr
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the complement, page 1 (25) under sort(-thingId) so the zzempty-* things lead the compared page: zzempty-markers (arr = []) and zzempty-shapes (markers holds [], defonly lacks arr) are excluded like every other feature-bearing thing (each has a feature lacking arr), so the page holds the 25 highest-sorting feature-less things.

cases.name: empty-wildcard-nullprop
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), JSON null carried by a pre-SB-02 fixture: nenull-nullvals (its ONLY feature f1 holds nullProp = null) can match only through the null branch; nenull-realvals and nenull-stringvals (a value) do not match; every other feature-bearing thing lacks nullProp and matches. Not crossed with allowlist #8: GetEmptyBsonVisitor builds the elemMatch under sudo too, so strict parity holds in all 9 situations.

cases.name: not-empty-wildcard-nullprop
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), the complement restricted to feature-bearing things so its two witnesses are on the compared page: nenull-realvals and nenull-stringvals (their only feature holds a value) are the ONLY matches; nenull-nullvals (null) and every thing with a feature lacking nullProp are excluded; the feature-less things (which match the bare not(...) vacuously) are cut by exists(features/*).

cases.name: empty-wildcard-secretcode
cases.comment: empty() wildcard Mongo-parity battery (SB-02), a property-level REVOKE in the wildcard auth chain ([<root>, /features, /id, /properties, /properties/secretcode] on a.f_id): under 'feature' (policy-graded, /features/lamp/properties/secretcode revoked) scalars-green matches through f1 (lacks secretcode; its lamp holds "s3cr3t", not empty), feature-agree/-disagree and the zzempty-graded-* through their visible f1; policy-full things are invisible to that subject. Under sudo every feature-bearing thing has a feature lacking secretcode.
